cards.title: 5x faster Edge Functions: V8 isolates to Firecracker MicroVMs

depth.text: Netlify says **Edge Functions** are about **five times faster** after moving them onto its own network

Warm invocations now cost **~5–6ms at median**, down from **25–40ms** on the previous infrastructure. Each function runs in its own **Firecracker MicroVM**, and requests stay inside Netlify’s network.

cards.camps: Two camps: skeptics say Netlify may have removed network hops rather than made execution faster; others say the old hosted runtime explains the latency and MicroVMs offer stronger isolation.

comments.text: I've been using SlicerVM extensively - which is Firecracker MicroVMs for the regular person (and for the irregular with their platform offering) - to run local 'edge' style workloads locally and securly. Agents, local dev CI, etc. It slotted in and replaced my proxmox vm orchestrator, and now I have secure and and fast vms on my laptop wherever I go. It also supports dockerfile style builds if…

Alex from Unikraft here! Happy to answer any questions about the microVM part of the story from our side. We also did a couple of technical write ups if you're interested: - https://unikraft.com/blog/netlify-edge-functions - https://unikraft.com/customer-stories/edge-functions-netlify

> In the past, requests went out to a hosted execution service. Today, they run on MicroVMs inside our own edge network — roughly 5x faster at the median. So, the execution itself might now be slower as far as we know, they just eliminated some networking from the mix? Misleading.
I'm having trouble understanding/believing this, given that Cloudflare Workers are also v8 isolates and run vastly faster than the 25-40ms that netlify says their isolates took...

All else being equal, v8 isolates should be lower latency than firecracker. As they mention, the v8 latency was because the v8 runtime was hosted externally. Firecracker has better security model.
